incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: HTTP appender in Logback posted to FraudController.authenticate; that method logged the request, recursing.

incidents.title: Lost updates in PaymentService.refund under parallel load
incidents.description: Concurrent callers of PaymentService.refund produced inconsistent cart totals. Read-modify-write without a lock allowed two threads to observe the same pre-state. 1500 affected records.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
int current = repo.getQuantity(sku);
repo.setQuantity(sku, current - qty); // no lock, lost update
incidents.root_cause: @Transactional removed from PaymentService.refund during a refactor, exposing the read-modify-write race.
incidents.resolution: Re-added @Transactional and added @Version optimistic locking on the entity.

incidents.title: Unhandled promise rejection in FraudScheduler.aggregate
incidents.description: Node warned on 'UnhandledPromiseRejection' for 2400 requests originating from FraudScheduler.aggregate. Errors silently dropped; clients saw hung connections.
incidents.root_cause: FraudScheduler.aggregate didn't await the inner promise — rejections escaped the try/catch.
incidents.resolution: Replaced create_task with awaited call; added error callback.

incidents.title: recommendations-service fell behind topic by 500 messages
incidents.description: A sudden traffic surge overwhelmed the single-threaded consumer in RecommendationsWorker.deserialize; lag alerts fired within 10 minutes.
incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: Per-message processing in RecommendationsWorker.deserialize includes an expensive ML call; latency > poll interval.

incidents.title: Inconsistent pagination cursor in PaymentWorker.render
incidents.description: ORDER BY non-unique column caused page 2+ to rehash order and skip items in PaymentWorker.render.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: return repo.findAll(Sort.by("createdAt")).page(n, size);
incidents.root_cause: Offset-based pagination used for mutating list; items inserted between pages cause drift.
incidents.resolution: Switched to keyset pagination: ORDER BY (created_at, id).

incidents.title: N+1 query in NotificationsWorker.persist blows up latency
incidents.description: NotificationsWorker.persist loads a collection then issues one DB call per item. With input sizes ~200, p99 crossed 8s. Evidence: trace span count scaling linearly with input size.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
for txn in user.transactions:
    score += risk_db.lookup(txn.id)  # N queries
incidents.root_cause: Lazy-loaded association triggers a SELECT per element inside NotificationsWorker.persist's loop.
incidents.resolution: Added JPA @EntityGraph to eager-fetch the association.

incidents.title: Contention on item table blocks UserService.authenticate
incidents.description: Postgres reported lock_wait_timeout on the item table during peak traffic. UserService.authenticate held a row lock while calling a remote service inside the same transaction.
incidents.root_cause: UserService.authenticate performs a network call inside the transaction boundary, holding locks far longer than needed.
incidents.resolution: Enforced a canonical lock-acquisition order across UserService.authenticate and the batch job.

incidents.title: CartService.addItem mishandles DST transition
incidents.description: Scheduled job in CartService.addItem fired at 01:00 local but skipped on DST-spring-forward day.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
LocalDateTime now = LocalDateTime.now(); // system-default TZ
repo.save(new Event(now)); // saved as UTC — off by offset
incidents.root_cause: CartService.addItem mixes LocalDateTime with Instant — implicit system-default TZ used in one branch.
incidents.resolution: Switched to Instant/UTC throughout; added lint rule banning LocalDateTime.now().

incidents.title: Enum value mismatch between notifications-service and sqs
incidents.description: NotificationsService.send received an enum value sqs had added but notifications-service did not know about. Deserialization threw; requests 500'd.
incidents.root_cause: sqs added the PENDING_REVIEW status; notifications-service was never updated.
incidents.resolution: Added default: return unknown() branch; emit metric on unseen enum.

incidents.title: Thundering herd hits snowflake when PaymentRepository.commit cache expires
incidents.description: Post-deploy cache flush caused all requests for popular SKUs to bypass cache and hit the primary DB simultaneously.
incidents.root_cause: PaymentRepository.commit uses naive cache-aside with no single-flight — concurrent misses all fetch from origin.
incidents.resolution: Added TTL jitter ±20% and per-key lock on cache miss.

incidents.title: Rate-limit amplification from FraudService.evaluate into postgres
incidents.description: FraudService.evaluate fan-out multiplied incoming request volume 12x into postgres. postgres returned 429s for 25 minutes. Customer-visible as slow checkouts.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
for item in request.items:
    dep.call(item)  # quota thrasher
incidents.root_cause: No request-coalescing in FraudService.evaluate; per-sub-item calls instead of batch API.
incidents.resolution: Added a token-bucket limiter at the client edge with 100 rps ceiling.

incidents.title: Cold-start latency in NotificationsProcessor.consume on notifications-service autoscale
incidents.description: New pods on notifications-service served p99 > 8s for first 60 seconds. JIT + cache warmup missing in NotificationsProcessor.consume.
incidents.root_cause: No readiness-probe warmup in notifications-service; autoscaler-added pods received traffic immediately.
incidents.resolution: Added 30s warmup phase with representative query replay on readiness probe.

incidents.title: InventoryService.release silently swallows downstream failures
incidents.description: Orders succeeded from the caller's perspective even when downstream catalog-service failed. A catch block in InventoryService.release logged the error at DEBUG but returned success.
incidents.root_cause: Generic catch (Exception) in InventoryService.release logged and continued instead of propagating.
incidents.resolution: Propagated failure as a domain exception; added contract test.

incidents.title: shipping-service heap grows unbounded in ShippingService.createLabel cache
incidents.description: A cache added to ShippingService.createLabel used request IDs as keys. Entries never expired. After 36h the retained size exceeded 2 GB.
incidents.root_cause: Unbounded cache in ShippingService.createLabel — no size cap, no TTL.
incidents.resolution: Switched to LRU with explicit capacity; added metric cache.size for alerting.

incidents.title: CartController.process scaling linearly with input size
incidents.description: CartController.process loads a collection then issues one DB call per item. With input sizes ~200, p99 crossed 8s. Evidence: trace span count scaling linearly with input size.
incidents.root_cause: Batch fetch helper removed during cleanup; CartController.process reverted to per-item lookup.
incidents.resolution: Batched into a single risk_db.lookup_batch(txn_ids) call.

incidents.title: CORS preflight failures on CartService.checkout endpoint
incidents.description: Wildcard CORS config tightened for security; legitimate marketing origin not allowlisted.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
@CrossOrigin(origins = "https://app.swagstore.com") // missed marketing subdomain
@PostMapping("/api/charge") public Response charge(...) { ... }
incidents.root_cause: CORS allowlist regex missed the marketing subdomain CartService.checkout serves.
incidents.resolution: Extended allowlist to cover all swagstore.com subdomains via regex; lint-rule banning wildcards.

incidents.title: Unknown field crashes AnalyticsWorker.authenticate JSON parse
incidents.description: AnalyticsWorker.authenticate crashed on messages from a newer producer that added a field. Jackson configured with FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=true.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
dec := json.NewDecoder(r)
dec.DisallowUnknownFields() // breaks on producer adding field
var msg Message
dec.Decode(&msg)
incidents.root_cause: AnalyticsWorker.authenticate used strict deserialization; broke compatibility when producer added a non-nullable field.
incidents.resolution: Relaxed to FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=false; documented forward-compat expectation.

incidents.title: Mutable default argument causes state bleed in UserService.authenticate
incidents.description: Every invocation of UserService.authenticate appended to the same shared list, producing cross-call leakage.
incidents.root_cause: Static List initializer in UserService.authenticate was shared by all instances.
incidents.resolution: Replaced static BUFFER with a per-request instance variable.

incidents.title: SearchResolver.dispatch serves stale record after config change
incidents.description: SearchResolver.dispatch served stale record values for up to 800 hours after the source was updated. Cache invalidation hook was removed during a cleanup.
incidents.root_cause: Index rebuild job cron-only; no event-driven invalidation.
incidents.resolution: Subscribed SearchResolver.dispatch to the update-event stream; TTL reduced to 5m.

incidents.title: Timeout cascade from stripe saturates PaymentService.charge
incidents.description: Ingress requests timed out because PaymentService.charge waited the full client timeout for stripe before returning. Retries amplified it.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
RestTemplate rt = new RestTemplate();
rt.getRequestFactory().setReadTimeout(30_000); // 30s — too generous
incidents.root_cause: No circuit breaker in front of stripe — slow failures consumed all worker threads.
incidents.resolution: Enforced timeout-budget rule: client timeout < ingress timeout / 2.

incidents.title: SQL injection protection regression in SearchWorker.enrich
incidents.description: A security audit flagged SearchWorker.enrich for concatenating user input into a SQL query. No confirmed exploits but disclosure deadline imposed.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: row := db.QueryRow("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" + email + "'") // SQLi
incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: Dynamic query builder escaped single quotes but not other metacharacters.

incidents.title: UserWorker.aggregate first-request latency crosses SLO
incidents.description: Post-deploy, cold-started instances of user-service handled traffic before UserWorker.aggregate had loaded its models.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
// no warmup queries on pod start
@PostConstruct public void init() { /* nothing */ }
incidents.root_cause: No readiness-probe warmup in user-service; autoscaler-added pods received traffic immediately.
incidents.resolution: Added 30s warmup phase with representative query replay on readiness probe.

incidents.title: PII leak through PaymentService.charge debug logs
incidents.description: A print-statement left from local testing exposed full card numbers in PaymentService.charge for PCI-scoped traffic.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: log.debug("charge req: {}", chargeRequest); // prints PAN
incidents.root_cause: Struct printed with %+v in PaymentService.charge, exposing sensitive fields.
incidents.resolution: Introduced a redact() helper + CI lint rule blocking %+v on request types.

incidents.title: Sensitive token logged in PaymentProcessor.resolve
incidents.description: Debug logging in PaymentProcessor.resolve included config.flags tokens for ~12 minutes. Compliance filed an incident; logs scrubbed retroactively.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: log.debug("charge req: {}", chargeRequest); // prints PAN
incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: Struct printed with %+v in PaymentProcessor.resolve, exposing sensitive fields.

incidents.title: Field typo in SearchService.query silently drops data
incidents.description: A field rename went through search-service but missed SearchService.query. Messages with the new field were dropped at serialization; messages with the old name silently passed through.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: return map[string]any{"user_Id": id} // typo
incidents.root_cause: Typo `user_Id` vs `userId` in SearchService.query's JSON emitter.
incidents.resolution: Added consumer-side strict validation on unknown/missing keys.

incidents.title: Circular service dependency involving InventoryHandler.match
incidents.description: A newly added call from InventoryHandler.match into rabbitmq triggered rabbitmq to call back into inventory-service, which looped through InventoryHandler.match again. Stack overflow after ~300 calls.
incidents.root_cause: rabbitmq added a synchronous callback to InventoryHandler.match, forming a cycle.
incidents.resolution: Refactored to injected interface; broke the tight Spring cycle.

incidents.title: Shared list default in CartGateway.serialize accumulates across calls
incidents.description: Calls to CartGateway.serialize started seeing data from previous calls. A default [] argument kept accumulating appends across invocations.
incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: Static List initializer in CartGateway.serialize was shared by all instances.

incidents.title: JWT verification drift in FraudService.evaluate
incidents.description: JWT signature verification in FraudService.evaluate fell back to HS256 when RS256 key lookup failed.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=["RS256", "HS256"])  # algorithm confusion
incidents.root_cause: Algorithm confusion — accepted HS256 tokens signed with the public RS256 key.
incidents.resolution: Pinned algorithm to RS256 explicitly; rejected unexpected algs.

incidents.title: Database migration rollback leaves order-service in broken state
incidents.description: Rollback of order-service left the schema mid-migration. Writes via OrderService.place hit 500s on missing column.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
@Column(name = "ext_id", nullable = false) // column not present after rollback
private String extId;
incidents.root_cause: Non-transactional DDL meant the failed migration left an orphaned column.
incidents.resolution: Added DOWN migration + test; rollout gated on migration success.

incidents.title: JWT verification drift in CatalogService.build
incidents.description: CatalogService.build accepted expired tokens for ~1500 minutes. Clock skew leeway widened by accident.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: JWT.require(algorithm).acceptLeeway(3600).build() // too permissive
incidents.root_cause: Leeway changed from 30s to 3600s in CatalogService.build via a "debug fix" that was never reverted.
incidents.resolution: Pinned algorithm to RS256 explicitly; rejected unexpected algs.

incidents.title: Unknown field crashes AnalyticsResolver.cache JSON parse
incidents.description: AnalyticsResolver.cache crashed on messages from a newer producer that added a field. Jackson configured with FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=true.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
dec := json.NewDecoder(r)
dec.DisallowUnknownFields() // breaks on producer adding field
var msg Message
dec.Decode(&msg)
incidents.root_cause: AnalyticsResolver.cache used strict deserialization; broke compatibility when producer added a non-nullable field.
incidents.resolution: Relaxed to FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=false; documented forward-compat expectation.

incidents.title: Cold-start latency in OrderController.build on order-service autoscale
incidents.description: New pods on order-service served p99 > 8s for first 60 seconds. JIT + cache warmup missing in OrderController.build.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
// no warmup queries on pod start
@PostConstruct public void init() { /* nothing */ }
incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: OrderController.build lazily loads models on first request; initialization takes 40s.

incidents.title: TLS handshake failures after cert expiry on payment-service
incidents.description: Expired intermediate cert caused TLS handshake failures on PaymentService.refund's egress to stripe. All downstream calls failed for 40 minutes.
incidents.root_cause_hypothesis: Pinned truststore not updated after stripe rotated its CA.

incidents.title: PaymentHandler.cache drops items across page boundaries
incidents.description: ORDER BY non-unique column caused page 2+ to rehash order and skip items in PaymentHandler.cache.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: return repo.findAll(Sort.by("createdAt")).page(n, size);
incidents.root_cause: Offset-based pagination used for mutating list; items inserted between pages cause drift.
incidents.resolution: Added id as tiebreaker to sort; cursor now stable.

incidents.title: order-service not reloaded after config change
incidents.description: OrderRepository.poll cached the config at boot; operators rotated the flag but order-service wasn't restarted.
incidents.offending_code_snippet: @Value("${api.key}") private String apiKey; // resolved once at boot
incidents.root_cause: OrderRepository.poll reads the secret once at boot; no refresh hook.
incidents.resolution: Moved secret lookup inside the request path; fetched from Vault per-minute cache.

incidents.title: InventoryService.reserve async callback swallows errors
incidents.description: Node warned on 'UnhandledPromiseRejection' for 120 requests originating from InventoryService.reserve. Errors silently dropped; clients saw hung connections.
incidents.root_cause: Fire-and-forget pattern in InventoryService.reserve with no .catch(); rejected promise unhandled.
incidents.resolution: Replaced create_task with awaited call; added error callback.

incidents.title: Timeout cascade from elasticsearch saturates UserWorker.refresh
incidents.description: elasticsearch latency went from 100ms to 4s. UserWorker.refresh's 5s client timeout held, but thread-pool starved; upstream callers started timing out too.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
RestTemplate rt = new RestTemplate();
rt.getRequestFactory().setReadTimeout(30_000); // 30s — too generous
incidents.root_cause: No circuit breaker in front of elasticsearch — slow failures consumed all worker threads.
incidents.resolution: Tightened elasticsearch client timeout to 2s; added Resilience4j circuit breaker.

incidents.title: PaymentGateway.rollback exceeded s3 quota during burst
incidents.description: A loop in PaymentGateway.rollback called s3 per sub-item. At p95 input size, quota tripped within 90 seconds.
incidents.root_cause: Rate limit config on the client side raised from 50 to 500 rps without coordination with s3 team.
incidents.resolution: Switched to s3.call_batch(items); reduced RPS 10x.

incidents.title: Kafka consumer lag on payment-service from PaymentService.charge bottleneck
incidents.description: A sudden traffic surge overwhelmed the single-threaded consumer in PaymentService.charge; lag alerts fired within 10 minutes.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
@KafkaListener(topics = ["product-updates"], concurrency = "1")
public void consume(Record r) { process(r); }
incidents.root_cause: Consumer concurrency set to 1; topic has 8 partitions but only 1 worker thread.
incidents.resolution: Increased consumer concurrency to 8; matched topic partition count.

incidents.title: CORS preflight failures on CartResolver.refresh endpoint
incidents.description: Browser clients couldn't reach CartResolver.refresh endpoint after a CORS config change. Preflight returned 403 for Origin: https://web.swagstore.com.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
@CrossOrigin(origins = "https://app.swagstore.com") // missed marketing subdomain
@PostMapping("/api/charge") public Response charge(...) { ... }
incidents.root_cause: CORS allowlist regex missed the marketing subdomain CartResolver.refresh serves.
incidents.resolution: Added marketing.swagstore.com to the allowlist; added integration test.

incidents.title: InventoryService.release serves stale shipment after config change
incidents.description: InventoryService.release served stale shipment values for up to 120 hours after the source was updated. Cache invalidation hook was removed during a cleanup.
incidents.root_cause: Index rebuild job cron-only; no event-driven invalidation.
incidents.resolution: Event-driven invalidation added on ConfigChanged events.

incidents.title: Catch-and-log in CartService.checkout masks real errors
incidents.description: Exceptions from sqs in CartService.checkout were swallowed by a generic catch (Exception). Bug lived undetected for weeks.
incidents.root_cause: Empty catch block left over from scaffolding.
incidents.resolution: Replaced generic catch with specific TransientException handling.

incidents.title: ReDoS in UserClient.authorize regex triggers CPU spike
incidents.description: A crafted input of 2kB hung a worker in UserClient.authorize for 30s. Regex exhibited catastrophic backtracking on nested quantifiers.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
Pattern p = Pattern.compile("^(a+)+$");
p.matcher(userInput).matches(); // catastrophic
incidents.root_cause: Unbounded quantifier in email validator in UserClient.authorize.
incidents.resolution: Replaced with a linear-time parser; banned user-input regex matching.

incidents.title: PaymentResolver.refresh regex causes request timeout on long input
incidents.description: CPU saturation on payment-service traced to a regex in PaymentResolver.refresh against user-supplied input.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
Pattern p = Pattern.compile("^(a+)+$");
p.matcher(userInput).matches(); // catastrophic
incidents.root_cause: Regex `^(a+)+$` in PaymentResolver.refresh backtracks exponentially on non-matching input.
incidents.resolution: Replaced with a linear-time parser; banned user-input regex matching.

incidents.title: RecommendationsGateway.render exceeded rabbitmq quota during burst
incidents.description: RecommendationsGateway.render fan-out multiplied incoming request volume 12x into rabbitmq. rabbitmq returned 429s for 25 minutes. Customer-visible as slow checkouts.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
for item in request.items:
    dep.call(item)  # quota thrasher
incidents.root_cause: No request-coalescing in RecommendationsGateway.render; per-sub-item calls instead of batch API.
incidents.resolution: Added a token-bucket limiter at the client edge with 100 rps ceiling.

incidents.title: Off-by-hours error in UserService.authenticate for non-UTC customers
incidents.description: Scheduled job in UserService.authenticate fired at 01:00 local but skipped on DST-spring-forward day.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
LocalDateTime now = LocalDateTime.now(); // system-default TZ
repo.save(new Event(now)); // saved as UTC — off by offset
incidents.root_cause: UserService.authenticate mixes LocalDateTime with Instant — implicit system-default TZ used in one branch.
incidents.resolution: Switched to Instant/UTC throughout; added lint rule banning LocalDateTime.now().

incidents.title: Off-by-hours error in RecommendationsRepository.fetch for non-UTC customers
incidents.description: Reports for 12 customers showed events attributed to the wrong day. RecommendationsRepository.fetch did date arithmetic in local time then wrote UTC.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
now = datetime.now()  # naive, system tz
repo.save(Event(now))  # assumed UTC downstream
incidents.root_cause: Forgot to convert to UTC before persisting. Works in dev (UTC container) but not prod (customer-local TZ).
incidents.resolution: Standardized on time.Now().UTC() and added a test with a non-UTC TZ container.

incidents.title: Global edge outage — regex catastrophic backtracking in WAF rule
incidents.description: A WAF rule containing the regex `(?:.*?.*)*A` was deployed globally. The pattern exhibited catastrophic backtracking on crafted inputs, driving CPU to 100% on every edge machine and taking the global network down for ~27 minutes. Originally documented at https://blog.cloudflare.com/details-of-the-cloudflare-outage-on-july-2-2019/.
incidents.root_cause: A new WAF rule regex `(?:.*?.*)*A` had exponential backtracking on some inputs; deploying it globally without gradual rollout pegged CPU across the fleet.
incidents.resolution: Kill-switched the global WAF, rolled back the rule, added per-regex CPU budget + staged rollout with automatic abort on CPU regression.

incidents.title: S3-style storage outage after an operator typo removed the wrong subsystem
incidents.description: A debugging playbook step intended to remove a small number of billing subsystem servers was run with a slightly wrong parameter, instead removing servers that backed the index and placement subsystems. Recovery required a full restart of dependent systems that had not been bounced at scale in years. Originally documented at https://aws.amazon.com/message/41926/.
incidents.root_cause: A runbook script lacked an allowlist check on the target group argument. The operator's command affected a broader set of hosts than intended, taking the index subsystem offline.
incidents.resolution: Added allowlist + minimum-capacity guardrail to the runbook tool; required approval for any call that would reduce capacity below a safety floor.

incidents.title: Dormant code path re-activated during partial deploy caused uncontrolled order flow
incidents.description: A feature flag repurposed an existing field to toggle new routing logic. Old dormant code behind that flag still existed on one of eight servers because the deploy missed it. When the flag flipped in production, that host executed the legacy path and sent unbounded orders in ~45 minutes. Originally documented at https://www.sec.gov/litigation/admin/2013/34-70694.pdf.
incidents.root_cause: A configuration flag was reused for a new meaning while the old code path remained on one of eight servers. The partial deploy left one server running dead code that interpreted the flag the old way.
incidents.resolution: Delete dead code before repurposing flags; enforce uniform deploys via health checks that verify commit SHA across the fleet before flipping flags.

incidents.title: Operator removed production database directory instead of replica
incidents.description: While trying to restore replication, an engineer ran `rm -rf` on what they thought was a stale replica but was actually the primary data directory. Most backup mechanisms turned out to be silently failing; recovery relied on a 6-hour-old LVM snapshot. Originally documented at https://about.gitlab.com/blog/2017/02/10/postmortem-of-database-outage-of-january-31/.
incidents.root_cause: Operator ran a destructive command against the primary database host by mistake; five of the service's backup methods were silently broken and had not been exercised.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
# no host check — runs wherever ssh lands
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/pgsql/data
sudo systemctl restart postgresql
incidents.resolution: Destructive commands must verify target host role; backups are now validated by scheduled restore drills, not presence of snapshot files.

incidents.title: Webhook retry storm amplified downstream outage 6x
incidents.description: A degraded downstream API returned 5xx for ~5 minutes. The webhook consumer's retry policy used fixed 1s intervals with no jitter or backoff; clients retried in lockstep and inflated incoming traffic 6× while the downstream was still recovering. Originally documented at https://stripe.com/blog/rate-limiters.
incidents.root_cause: Retry policy had neither exponential backoff nor jitter; every client retried at the same wall-clock second, hammering the recovering downstream.
incidents.resolution: Exponential backoff with full jitter; circuit breaker that trips after a sustained 5xx window and sheds retries for ~30s.

incidents.title: Kinesis-style service breakdown from OS thread limit hit during scale-up
incidents.description: Adding front-end capacity pushed total OS threads above a soft configuration limit. Connections to backend shards began failing, which cascaded into every downstream consumer because shard state was required at request time. Originally documented at https://aws.amazon.com/message/11201/.
incidents.root_cause: OS-level thread limit was set assuming historical fleet size; capacity growth exceeded that implicit limit during routine scale-up.
incidents.resolution: Replace per-shard threads with a shared NIO pool; monitor thread count as a first-class metric with alerts well before OS limits.

incidents.title: Single customer config flipped a latent nil-pointer across the entire edge fleet
incidents.description: A customer pushed a valid configuration change that triggered a dormant bug which had been shipped weeks earlier. The bug caused the edge process to panic on startup globally within seconds. Originally documented at https://www.fastly.com/blog/summary-of-june-8-outage.
incidents.root_cause: Dormant bug in config-parsing path: a specific valid customer shape dereferenced a nil map; global rollout surfaced it on every POP at once.
incidents.resolution: Add nil-map guards; validate configs in a canary POP before global rollout; roll out config changes in staged waves rather than fleet-wide.

incidents.title: Work-from-home tidal wave exhausted WebSocket connection limits
incidents.description: A large traffic surge exhausted a connection-tracking table on load balancers. Retries from disconnected clients compounded the problem by landing on the same subset of healthy hosts, creating a thundering herd. Originally documented at https://slack.engineering/slacks-outage-on-january-4th-2021/.
incidents.root_cause: Connection-tracking tables sized for historical traffic; reconnect logic lacked randomized backoff, causing synchronized reconnect storms.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
# all clients retry at the same second — thundering herd
while not self.connected:
    time.sleep(1)
    self.connect()
incidents.resolution: Randomized exponential backoff for reconnects; auto-scale connection-tracking capacity; spread reconnect fan-out across all healthy nodes.

incidents.title: Authentication failures cascaded from a quota service running out of storage
incidents.description: The user-identity quota tracking system exhausted allocated storage after a migration left old quota entries behind. Quota checks started failing closed, which meant no user could authenticate. Originally documented at https://status.cloud.google.com/incident/zall/20013.
incidents.root_cause: Quota-tracking storage filled because cleanup of stale entries was disabled during a migration; the auth dependency then failed closed rather than degrade.
incidents.resolution: Auth now fails open against a cached quota when the quota service is unavailable; retention policies are active during migrations.

incidents.title: Scheduled job fired at wrong hour after DST boundary timezone off-by-one
incidents.description: A nightly reindex job used a naive datetime without timezone info. After the DST transition it fired an hour earlier than intended, overlapping peak query traffic and driving p99 search latency to 8s. Originally documented at https://status.cloud.google.com/products/functions.
incidents.root_cause: Scheduler computed the next run from a naive local-time datetime; DST boundary shifted execution into a high-traffic window.
incidents.resolution: All scheduled jobs now compute next-run in UTC and convert explicitly for display; added DST-crossing unit tests.

incidents.title: Connection pool exhaustion from slow downstream under marketing spike
incidents.description: A marketing campaign doubled request volume. Downstream risk-ML service slowed to ~800ms p99; callers' fixed-size HTTP pools saturated and every subsequent request failed with a pool-timeout. Originally documented at https://eng.lyft.com/envoy-dynamic-forward-proxy-at-lyft-f61c5ddc7e83.
incidents.root_cause: HTTP connection pool sized for p99 of 100ms; latency regression in the downstream caused in-flight concurrency to exceed pool size.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
# fixed pool size, no timeout budget
pool = HTTPPool(size=32, timeout=None)
resp = pool.post('/score', json=payload)
incidents.resolution: Bounded request timeouts + concurrency limit + graceful degradation to a cached-risk score when the pool saturates.

incidents.title: Memcache thundering herd on hot key after cache-node failure
incidents.description: A cache node was drained for maintenance. The hottest key (~40k QPS) immediately missed on every replica simultaneously, and every caller stampeded to the database with the same query. Originally documented at https://blog.twitter.com/engineering/en_us/a/2015/caching-with-twemcache.
incidents.root_cause: Cache-miss path was synchronous with no single-flight coordination; every concurrent reader issued the same backend query.
incidents.resolution: Wrap cache-miss loads in a single-flight coalescer; add short-TTL negative cache for misses; stagger evictions when draining a node.

incidents.title: Paging retry loop amplified alert traffic 50x
incidents.description: A downstream notification gateway returned 502 for 90 seconds. The paging worker retried every failed delivery every 100ms for the full duration, turning a short blip into a self-inflicted DDoS that delayed real alerts by ~18 minutes. Originally documented at https://www.pagerduty.com/resources/learn/post-mortem-incident-report/.
incidents.root_cause: Retry logic had no backoff, no max-attempts cap, no circuit breaker; every failed send re-queued instantly.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
while True:
    r = gateway.send(alert)
    if r.ok: break
    time.sleep(0.1)  # 100ms; no cap
incidents.resolution: Cap retries at 5 with exponential backoff; circuit breaker trips after a sustained 5xx window; dead-letter queue for undeliverable alerts.

incidents.title: DNS provider outage took down edge resolution for all customers
incidents.description: A backbone configuration change propagated a route that discarded internal DNS traffic. Because every edge POP depended on the same resolver plane, the failure was global within seconds. Originally documented at https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-outage-on-july-17-2020/.
incidents.root_cause: A router configuration change introduced a more-specific prefix that black-holed DNS traffic globally; no staged rollout.
incidents.resolution: Network config changes now go through canary POP first; automated rollback when DNS success rate drops below SLO for 30s.

incidents.title: Database network partition caused 24h stale-data window for some users
incidents.description: A 43-second network partition between database replication endpoints caused the orchestrator to promote a replica in another region. Divergent writes had to be manually reconciled; some user data appeared stale for ~24 hours. Originally documented at https://github.blog/2018-10-30-oct21-post-incident-analysis/.
incidents.root_cause: Orchestrator's failover policy prioritized availability over consistency; a brief partition caused promotion before data could drain.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
if primary_unreachable_for_seconds > 30:
    promote(find_replica())  # no drain-check, no lag gate
incidents.resolution: Promotion now requires replication-lag < 1s and explicit human ack for cross-region failover; writes block rather than silently diverge.

incidents.title: Public-bucket misconfiguration exposed internal test data
incidents.description: An object-storage bucket used for test data was created with default-public ACL by a CI job; it went unreviewed for weeks. No production secrets leaked but the exposure prompted a company-wide audit. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: CI bucket-creation script did not set private ACL explicitly and relied on default provider behavior, which had changed to public in a minor update.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
# ACL not specified — default is provider-dependent
s3.create_bucket(Bucket=name)
# forgot: s3.put_bucket_acl(Bucket=name, ACL='private')
incidents.resolution: CI role cannot create buckets without an explicit private ACL; weekly scan for publicly-readable buckets alerts security.

incidents.title: TLS certificate expired on weekend with no automated renewal
incidents.description: A TLS certificate for the internal payments API expired Saturday 02:00 UTC. Automated renewal had silently failed three weeks earlier because an IAM credential rotated; no one was paged. The cert expiry manifested as handshake failures across every caller. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Renewal job failed silently after credential rotation; no alert on days-to-expiry for internal certificates.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
# exit 0 even if renewal fails — logs only
renew_cert || echo 'renew failed' >> /var/log/certs.log
incidents.resolution: Renewal job pages on non-zero exit; monitor days-to-expiry as a first-class metric with alerts at 14/7/2 days.

incidents.title: Leaked CI secret in branch pipeline allowed unauthorized runner execution
incidents.description: A CI variable marked as non-protected was echoed in a merge-request pipeline log. The token had write access to the runner registry. Bot scanners found the leaked token within an hour and registered a malicious runner. Originally documented at https://about.gitlab.com/blog/2020/10/29/postmortem-of-kubernetes-api-failures/.
incidents.root_cause: CI variable was configured without the 'protected' flag, so it was exposed to pull-request pipelines from arbitrary branches; log masking did not cover it.
incidents.offending_code_snippet:
# echo for debugging, token not masked
script:
  - echo "runner token: $RUNNER_TOKEN"
  - ./build.sh
incidents.resolution: All CI secrets now marked protected + masked; runner tokens rotated on every merge; pipeline lint refuses echo of secret-prefixed variables.

incidents.title: Memory leak from unbounded feature cache crashed recommenders nightly
incidents.description: The recommender's feature cache was never trimmed; it grew until the process was OOM-killed nightly around 03:00 UTC. Restarts were automatic but cold-cache latency spiked for ~10 minutes each time. Originally documented at https://basecamp.com/gettingreal.
incidents.root_cause: Feature cache used an unbounded dict keyed by user_id; no eviction policy, so memory grew monotonically.
incidents.resolution: Replaced with LRU cache sized by byte budget; emits eviction-rate metric.

incidents.title: Datadog agent config change caused 10x metric cardinality explosion
incidents.description: A tag was added that embedded a user-supplied request-id into every custom metric. Cardinality exploded from ~50k series to ~5M in under an hour, throttling metric ingestion and blinding every downstream alert. Originally documented at https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/engineering/2023-03-08-9/.
incidents.root_cause: Tag expression used an unbounded request field as a tag value; the metrics backend rate-limited the tenant before the mistake was caught.
incidents.resolution: CI lints for high-cardinality tag expressions; telemetry sampler drops request_id-shaped values unless explicitly allowlisted.

incidents.title: Deadlock under concurrent stock updates from missing row-level lock
incidents.description: Two concurrent checkouts both read the same SKU's quantity, decremented locally, and wrote back. The last write won and oversold ~40 units. The race window was narrow but hit reliably during peak. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Quantity update used read-modify-write without a row-level lock or optimistic concurrency check.
incidents.resolution: Wrap in `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` transaction or use atomic `UPDATE ... SET qty = qty - ?` with affected-row check.

incidents.title: Queue worker lost messages on SIGTERM due to missing graceful shutdown
incidents.description: During a rolling deploy, worker containers received SIGTERM but killed in-flight handlers without re-queueing. Approximately 1,200 orders had their post-charge side effects (emails, fulfillment) dropped silently. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Worker loop ignored SIGTERM; kubelet force-killed after grace period, orphaning in-flight messages whose visibility timeout expired.
incidents.resolution: Install SIGTERM handler that stops poll loop, waits for in-flight handlers to complete within 25s (grace period), then nacks remainder.

incidents.title: Index rebuild ran twice after cron overlap, spiking disk to 98%
incidents.description: The nightly index rebuild started taking longer as corpus grew. Two runs overlapped and both wrote to separate temp indices; disk hit 98% and rejected new writes for 25 minutes. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Cron had no mutex; second invocation did not detect the first was still running; temp-index cleanup was at end-of-job.
incidents.resolution: Filesystem lockfile + PID check; per-run disk budget; abort + alert if previous run is still active at next scheduled tick.

incidents.title: Session cookie logic broke after Chrome SameSite default change
incidents.description: After Chrome rolled out `SameSite=Lax` by default, cross-site POSTs carrying the session cookie were silently dropped. Login-from-email-link flow broke for ~18% of users for 36 hours before the root cause was identified. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Session cookie was set without SameSite; browser default flipped to Lax, which strips the cookie on cross-site POST.
incidents.resolution: Explicitly set `SameSite=None; Secure` where cross-site POST is required; integration tests across Chrome/Safari/Firefox default policies.

incidents.title: R2-style regex in access rule caused CPU hot-loop on object names
incidents.description: A new object-storage access rule regex exhibited superlinear time on long object names. Bulk-list operations for one tenant caused 100% CPU on the evaluating workers for 6 minutes, throttling that region. Originally documented at https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-incident-on-february-2024-02-04/.
incidents.root_cause: Access-rule regex had nested quantifiers that could evaluate in O(n^3) for long object names with repeated separators.
incidents.resolution: Replaced the regex with an explicit linear matcher; added regex linter in CI that rejects nested quantifiers.

incidents.title: Secrets rotation shipped with stale value in encrypted config blob
incidents.description: A scheduled secret rotation updated the secrets store but the deployed pod image embedded the old value in an encrypted config blob that was read once at boot. New pods picked up the new value; old pods kept using the old value until restart. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Config layer read secrets once at boot and cached indefinitely; rotation did not trigger a rolling restart.
incidents.resolution: Secret loader now subscribes to rotation events and refreshes in-place; rotation runbook includes a rolling restart as a final step.

incidents.title: Serialization breaking change deployed ahead of consumer update
incidents.description: A field was renamed in the internal wire schema. The producer rolled out first; downstream consumers that hadn't picked up the client library version threw deserialization errors for every event, filling dead-letter queues for ~4 hours. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Wire schema had no versioning or forward-compatibility discipline; rename was treated as a compile-time refactor rather than a wire break.
incidents.resolution: Added schema registry with compatibility check in CI; renames require a two-phase rollout (emit both names → migrate consumers → drop old name).

incidents.title: Feature-flag SDK fell back to default when control plane returned 500
incidents.description: The feature-flag control plane experienced a 90-second outage. The SDK fell back to compile-time defaults, which had long diverged from production values. Multiple experiments silently flipped on for 100% of traffic. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: SDK fallback used stale compile-time defaults instead of the last-seen server value; the cache had been disabled months earlier 'to save memory'.
incidents.resolution: SDK persists last-seen values to local disk and uses those on control-plane failure; defaults reserved for first-ever boot only.

incidents.title: Model update regressed precision — fraud false-positives blocked legit orders
incidents.description: A retrained fraud model went to 100% of traffic after A/B reported neutral ROC-AUC. Precision at the chosen threshold had dropped 4pp, which was within ROC noise but blocked ~2,300 legitimate orders before rollback. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Rollout gate evaluated only aggregate ROC-AUC, not precision at the operating point actually used in production.
incidents.resolution: Rollout gate now evaluates precision and recall at the production threshold on a holdout set; auto-rollback on >1pp precision drop in the first hour.

incidents.title: Third-party SDK blocked event loop on startup health check
incidents.description: A tracing SDK performed a synchronous network call from a static initializer. When the collector was slow, startup blocked for 60s; the liveness probe failed and Kubernetes restarted pods in a loop, holding shipping traffic at 50% for 20 minutes. Originally documented at https://github.com/danluu/post-mortems.
incidents.root_cause: Blocking call in a static init path; no timeout; liveness probe had no grace period for startup I/O.
incidents.resolution: Moved SDK init off the startup path; added 5s timeout on collector handshake; liveness probe uses a dedicated fast path that doesn't wait on tracing.
